title: Accuracy of parsimony reconstruction under a molecular clock
decision_reason: Explicit source conjecture and independently authored specialist corroboration for r>4; later and potentially conflicting results compared at their actual scope; duplicate and separated A40 reviews passed.

problem_fingerprint.objects: A finite rooted binary phylogenetic tree with at least two labelled leaves; each edge has a finite nonnegative length; every root-to-leaf path has the same length H. An alphabet of r states, r >= 5.
problem_fingerprint.model: Neyman symmetric r-state continuous-time substitution model, with uniform root state and conditionally independent evolution down distinct branches. Normalize total departure rate to one: Q_ii=-1 and Q_ij=1/(r-1) for i != j.
problem_fingerprint.edge_transition: For edge length l, diagonal probability is 1/r+(r-1)/r*exp(-r*l/(r-1)); each specified off-diagonal probability is (1-exp(-r*l/(r-1)))/r.
problem_fingerprint.observation: One character: the random state at every leaf of the known tree. No repeated-site asymptotic limit or tree-topology estimation.
problem_fingerprint.estimator: Start with singleton leaf-state sets. At each internal vertex take the child-set intersection when nonempty, otherwise their union. Choose the root estimate uniformly from the final nonempty set.
problem_fingerprint.observable: Accuracy = probability that the estimator equals the actual root state, including both character generation and uniform tie-breaking.
problem_fingerprint.quantifiers: For every integer r >= 5 and every such finite tree and equal-height length assignment, including zero edge lengths, does accuracy exceed or equal 1/r+(r-1)/r*exp(-r*H/(r-1))?
problem_fingerprint.conclusion: The all-leaf Fitch estimator is at least as accurate as the state at any single leaf, whose conservation probability is the displayed common-height expression.
problem_fingerprint.normalization_checks: Herbst-Fischer use p_e for the probability of a transition to one specified different state. Herbst-Li-Steel use total change probability (r-1)*p_e. The displayed generator follows the latter expected-substitution-length convention.
problem_fingerprint.scope_limits: One conjecture across all alphabet sizes; r=2,3,4 are proved cases. No arbitrary-subset monotonicity, unequal root-to-leaf heights, asymmetric substitution rates, or deterministic/adversarial tie-breaking is asserted.

resolution_scope_comparisons.proposed_scope: Equal root-to-leaf lengths, all leaves versus a single leaf.
resolution_scope_comparisons.result_scope: Nearest-leaf counterexamples use unequal root-to-leaf distances. Subset counterexamples compare more than one retained leaf.
resolution_scope_comparisons.assessment: Neither contradicts the displayed clock/single-leaf inequality.

resolution_scope_comparisons.result_scope: Two, four and three states, respectively.
resolution_scope_comparisons.assessment: Solved cases explicitly omitted; no alphabet-size splitting into extra entries.

resolution_scope_comparisons.result_scope: All-state Fitch-set inequalities imply accuracy at least 1/r.
resolution_scope_comparisons.assessment: q_r(H)>1/r for finite H; the theorem does not provide the required stronger benchmark.

resolution_scope_comparisons.proposed_scope: Clock-tree Fitch accuracy versus common leaf accuracy.
resolution_scope_comparisons.result_scope: Coin-toss accuracy equals the leaf benchmark in clock trees for all r. Fitch dominates coin toss as a theorem only for r=2; general r is conjectural.
resolution_scope_comparisons.assessment: The conjectural all-tree comparison would imply this entry, but is not a proved resolution; no separate count.

resolution_scope_comparisons.proposed_scope: Unconditional expectation over all model-generated characters.
resolution_scope_comparisons.result_scope: Exact root recovery conditional on a deterministic weighted substitution-spectrum bound.
resolution_scope_comparisons.assessment: The event hypothesis is not automatic; this does not give the unconditional bound.

resolution_scope_comparisons.proposed_scope: Finite arbitrary clock trees and r>=5, benchmark q_r(H).
resolution_scope_comparisons.result_scope: Two-state model only. RW21 imposes a weighted branching condition to beat 1/2 uniformly over finite cutsets of an infinite tree; ZSYL10 strengthens the finite two-state bound.
resolution_scope_comparisons.assessment: Wrong alphabet range; RW21 also changes benchmark and limit regime.

resolution_scope_comparisons.proposed_scope: Probability of correctly estimating a random ancestral state.
resolution_scope_comparisons.result_scope: Minimum number of leaves bearing a designated color needed for a prescribed Fitch root set on a completely balanced tree.
resolution_scope_comparisons.assessment: Odd-state counterexample disproves a different combinatorial recurrence. It is not a stochastic-accuracy counterexample.

resolution_scope_comparisons.proposed_scope: Known rooted topology, random single character, r>=5.
resolution_scope_comparisons.result_scope: Binary alignments comprising all characters of specified parsimony score; compare unrooted topologies in an NNI neighborhood.
resolution_scope_comparisons.assessment: Both the positive result and counterexamples address reconstruction of topology, not this estimator's root-state accuracy.

resolution_scope_comparisons.proposed_scope: Probabilities realizable by actual clock trees.
resolution_scope_comparisons.result_scope: Negative formal polynomial values without a realizing tree; only certain small-tree cases proved.
resolution_scope_comparisons.assessment: The author explicitly does not claim a counterexample. The affected r=3,4 cases are subsequently proved by HF18.

resolution_scope_comparisons.proposed_scope: All finite clock trees and their finite-height leaf accuracy.
resolution_scope_comparisons.result_scope: Equal-edge comb examples are non-clock. Hennigian combs and balanced-tree analyses address special families and limiting/numerical behavior.
resolution_scope_comparisons.assessment: Convergence to 1/r as height grows does not contradict a finite-H bound whose right-hand side also tends to 1/r. No matching finite-tree counterexample or all-tree theorem is provided.

resolution_scope_comparisons.proposed_scope: Fitch root-state probability versus one leaf for every finite clock tree.
resolution_scope_comparisons.result_scope: Theorem 2 compares root and internal nodes; Theorem 3/Proposition 4 compare methods in a two-state model; Theorem 6 averages over growing Yule trees and contrasts root and random internal nodes.
resolution_scope_comparisons.assessment: Different observables, model restrictions or asymptotic/averaging quantifiers; no all-r finite-tree single-leaf resolution.

duplicate_review.method: Inventory of all active titles and models from the established baseline; current rg search for Fitch, ancestral-state, phylogenetic, ultrametric, molecular-clock, parsimony and Neyman terminology across active pages, metadata, drafts and candidate records. nearest.difference: Random selected-population ancestry and rescaled partition-process convergence, not estimating a finite-state root on a fixed known tree.
Worst-case exact string recovery from repeated deletion-channel samples, not one tree-indexed character and a prescribed estimator.
Optimizing balanced measurable Gaussian partitions under correlated noise, not the accuracy of a fixed Fitch recursion under a finite-state tree process.
